live_web_research.page_text: [2610.00232] Constant-Memory Recall: Learned Associations in a Fixed Matrix State Skip to main content Search arXiv Press Enter to search · Advanced search --> Computer Science > Machine Learning arXiv:2610.00232 (cs) [Submitted on 23 Sep 2026] Title: Constant-Memory Recall: Learned Associations in a Fixed Matrix State Authors: Samuel Larson View a PDF of the paper titled Constant-Memory Recall: Learned Associations in a Fixed Matrix State, by Samuel Larson View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Fixed-size recurrent memory limits storage growth during inference, but successful recall depends on the task and training. We study a small DeltaNet variant with fixed token-specific key biases, trained to remember 32 new key-value pairings per sequence. With 32 KiB of recurrent matrix state, it achieves 99.95% mean accuracy across three training seeds when choosing among the sequence's values. Recall remains near perfect when filler extends the pre-query context to 1,798 tokens without adding pairings. Zeroing the first memory block removes this recall. An exploratory 48-pair test remains near chance after one quarter of the primary training budget and does not locate a capacity limit. Parameter-matched vector and Transformer baselines remain near chance, including the Transformer after additional training searches. This unresolved baseline failure prevents a memory-efficiency comparison. We study a small DeltaNet variant with fixed token-specific key biases, trained to remember 32 new key-value pairings per sequence. This unresolved baseline failure prevents a memory-efficiency comparison. selected_records.title: Constant-Memory Recall: Learned Associations in a Fixed Matrix State

article.body:
Constant-Memory Recall paper reports a narrow DeltaNet test

Samuel Larson’s arXiv paper, “Constant-Memory Recall: Learned Associations in a Fixed Matrix State,” studies a small DeltaNet variant with fixed token-specific key biases—not an autonomous-vehicle system. Trained on 32 key–value pairs per sequence, it achieved 99.95% mean recall accuracy across three seeds using 32 KiB of recurrent matrix state. Recall stayed near perfect with filler extending the pre-query context to 1,798 tokens. An exploratory 48-pair test remained near chance after one-quarter of the primary training budget; it did not establish a capacity limit. Vector and Transformer baselines also stayed near chance, preventing a memory-efficiency comparison. The paper reports no vehicle trials, operational domain, road-safety data, deployment, regulatory approval or transport-service implications.
